To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the C-terminal half (residues 150-280) of the transcriptional cofactor human PC4 binds DNA with high affinity and specificity and that the interaction with DNA is mediated by simultaneous contact with both opposing strands.
the C-terminal domain binds with high affinity to ssDNA and heteroduplexes, that both single strands are contacted by the PC4 C terminus, and that the C terminus destabilizes dsDNA.

the C-terminal half domain of PC4 exhibits high-affinity binding to ssDNA, that this binding requires the juxtaposition of single-stranded segments of at least eight nucleotides, and that both the PC2 C-terminal domain and intact PC4 destabilizes dsDNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of a novel DNA-binding mode for the PC4 C-terminus that is distinct from previously reported interactions of PC4 with dsDNA and TBP.

a new class of ssDNA-binding proteins that are capable of high-affinity interaction with single strands in a juxtaposed fashion and that destabilize dsDNA, which may have important consequences for the function of PC4 as a transcriptional coactivators.
the identification of novel DNA binding properties of the PC4 transcriptional coactivators, which are likely to contribute to their function in transcriptional regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ssDNA binding of PC4 is not a simple binding of a ssDNA, but rather the binding of two ssDNAs in close proximity to each other.
PC4 binds ssDNA, and in the presence of an activator, PC4 may bind to the promoter and stabilize the activator-TFIID complex by binding to the activator.
PC4 ssDNA interactions are not only of importance in the formation of the PC4-TFIIA-TBP complex, but that they may also be of relevance in other aspects of the initiation process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PC4 has evolved a dual DNA-binding mode that allows it to interact with the TATA-box and with upstream-binding factors in a manner that is consistent with the observed stabilization of the TFIID/TFIIA/TATA-box complex.
PC4 is a versatile protein with multiple functions that are all related to the regulation of transcription.
PC4 has a unique DNA binding mode and that its interaction with DNA may involve a number of different mechanisms, depending on the specific DNA structure and the functional context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ssDNA binding activity of PC4 is a general property of the C-terminal domain that is not restricted to the interaction of this fragment with a heteroduplet structure.
the C-terminal domain has a dual role in transcriptional regulation, which may be of general importance in transcription.
the PC4 C-terminus is a high-affinity ssDNA binding protein with the ability to destabilize dsDNA, and that these properties may be involved in the enhancement of transcription.
